title: UPDATE: PayPal Plans $1.5B in AI Savings to Support Future Profit Growth
summary:
PayPal aims to cut costs by $1.5B over the next few years by deploying AI agents in customer service as part of a plan to drive long-term profitability. CEO Enrique Lores forecast that the company can achieve "sustainable double-digit" non-GAAP earnings growth in the medium term, citing a strategy that combines share buybacks and transaction margin expansion with ongoing operational efficiency.

The outlook follows a third-quarter report in which PayPal raised its full-year adjusted earnings per share guide to approximately $5.60, up from $5.38. While the company posted an adjusted EPS of $1.45, beating the $1.31 analyst estimate, its quarterly revenue of $8.58B missed the $8.71B forecast. The profit targets are underpinned by a reduction of more than 2,000 jobs this year, including over 25% of management layers, while its Venmo unit reported that quarterly payment volume grew 12% to $97.4B.
